title: Length of the Longest Alphabetical Continuous Substring
spaceBreakdown:
- int variables n, maxLen, cur, i: constant → O(1)
- no containers, no recursion, no extra allocation
- not counted: input string s
approach: Scan the string once, maintaining the length of the current run of alphabetically consecutive characters. Two adjacent characters extend the run exactly when s[i] == s[i-1] + 1; otherwise the run resets to 1. Track the maximum run length seen. This is correct because any valid substring is a maximal run of such adjacent pairs, and every such run is itself a valid alphabetical continuous substring.
hints: For a substring to be alphabetical continuous, what exact relationship must each character have with the one immediately before it? The alphabet has only 26 letters, so the answer can never exceed 26.
Use a single pass with a running counter that grows when s[i] == s[i-1]+1 and resets to 1 otherwise. In "abcde", since 'b'=='a'+1, 'c'=='b'+1, and so on, the counter climbs from 1 to 5.

**Smallest input** - a single character with no adjacent pair to compare.
`Input: s = "a"` → `Expected: 1`
⚠️ Bug: initializing maxLen to 0 and updating it only inside the loop body → returns 0

**All equal** - no two adjacent characters differ by exactly +1.
`Input: s = "aaaa"` → `Expected: 1`
⚠️ Bug: using `s[i] >= s[i-1]` instead of `s[i] == s[i-1]+1` → returns 4

**Reverse sorted** - every adjacent pair decreases.
`Input: s = "zyxw"` → `Expected: 1`
⚠️ Bug: using `abs(s[i]-s[i-1]) == 1` instead of the exact +1 check → returns 4

**Run never resets** - the entire string is one continuous run, so the else branch never executes.
`Input: s = "abc"` → `Expected: 3`
⚠️ Bug: updating maxLen only inside the else (reset) branch → returns 0

**Full alphabet** - the maximum achievable answer.
`Input: s = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"` → `Expected: 26`
⚠️ Bug: capping the answer at 25 (off-by-one on the alphabet size) → returns 25

followUps.q: What if 'z' followed by 'a' is also considered consecutive (circular alphabet)?
followUps.a: Change the extension condition to `(s[i] == s[i-1]+1) || (s[i-1]=='z' && s[i]=='a')`. Time stays O(n), space stays O(1).

followUps.q: Return the longest alphabetical continuous substring itself instead of its length.
followUps.a: Track the start index of the current run alongside its length; when a new maximum is found, record (start, length). At the end return s.substr(bestStart, bestLen). Time O(n), space O(1) auxiliary (the returned substring is output).

followUps.q: Characters arrive one at a time in a stream and you must report the current maximum after each character.
followUps.a: Keep the previous character, the current run length, and the running maximum as state. On each new character apply the same extend/reset logic and emit the maximum. Time O(1) per character, space O(1).
